0EC5F7A0:EE:00F56030.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
0EC5F7A0:EE:00F56030.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

20E7CC63:EE:00F52020.notes:
Controls how fast the freecam moves while in freecam mode (float, default ~1.0).
Left stick pans, right stick rotates, Circle moves forward, Square moves backward.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify in PCSX2 with Debug > Memory Search.

20E7CC63:EE:00F52030.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
20E7CC63:EE:00F52030.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

278700A0:EE:00B82090.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
278700A0:EE:00B82090.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

399A49CA:EE:00B81090.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
399A49CA:EE:00B81090.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

3F9E2D59:EE:00F59030.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
3F9E2D59:EE:00F59030.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

4A8DE991:EE:00F54030.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
4A8DE991:EE:00F54030.game: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus (SCUS-97198)
4A8DE991:EE:00F54030.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

5767E7EA:EE:00B80090.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
5767E7EA:EE:00B80090.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

6A2B7C19:EE:00B80090.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
6A2B7C19:EE:00B80090.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

7AC3B4F3:EE:00B81090.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
7AC3B4F3:EE:00B81090.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

8A9CE7E6:EE:00F52010.description: Freecam enable — decouples camera from player/car for cinematic or debug use
8A9CE7E6:EE:00F52010.notes:
Set to 1 to enable freecam (camera detaches from player/car), 0 to disable.

8A9CE7E6:EE:00F52020.notes:
Controls how fast the freecam moves while in freecam mode (float, default ~1.0).
Left stick pans, right stick rotates, Circle moves forward, Square moves backward.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify in PCSX2 with Debug > Memory Search.

8A9CE7E6:EE:00F52030.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
8A9CE7E6:EE:00F52030.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

A39517AB:EE:00F57030.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
A39517AB:EE:00F57030.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6010.description: LOD far distance — distance at which lowest-quality LOD kicks in
B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6010.notes: Float. Larger values keep higher-detail models visible at greater distance. Estimated.

value_map.457A0000: 4000.0 — extended far LOD (higher quality at distance)

B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6014.description: Mipmap enable flag — enables or disables mipmap texture filtering
B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6014.notes: Boolean flag. 0 = disable mipmaps (can improve sharpness at cost of aliasing). Estimated.

B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6018.description: Depth of field enable flag — toggles the depth-of-field blur effect
B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6018.notes: Boolean flag in the post-processing configuration. 0 = disabled (crisp), 1 = enabled. Estimated address.

B1C3B0A5:EE:003B601C.description: Depth of field intensity — strength of the out-of-focus blur

B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6020.description: Post-processing enable flag — master toggle for post-process effects
B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6020.notes: Boolean. Disabling turns off all post-process effects (bloom, tone-mapping, etc.). Estimated address.

B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6024.description: Bloom / glow intensity — strength of the bloom/HDR glow effect

B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6028.description: Primary draw distance — main camera render distance for world geometry
B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6028.notes: Float (world units). Larger values render geometry further away. Estimated.

B1C3B0A5:EE:003B602C.description: Far draw distance — secondary (far clip) render distance
B1C3B0A5:EE:003B602C.notes: Float (world units). Controls the far clipping plane distance. Estimated.

B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6030.description: Object fade distance — distance at which objects start to pop in/out
B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6030.notes: Float. Higher values make objects appear at greater distances. Estimated.

B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6034.description: Shadow draw distance — how far away shadows are rendered
B1C3B0A5:EE:003B6034.notes: Float. Larger values cast shadows at greater range. Estimated.

Controls how fast the freecam moves while in freecam mode (float, default ~1.0).

B9D90F75:EE:00F54030.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
B9D90F75:EE:00F54030.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

C4F9E878:EE:00B80080.notes:
Controls how fast the freecam moves while in freecam mode (float, default ~1.0).
Left stick pans, right stick rotates, Circle moves forward, Square moves backward.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify in PCSX2 with Debug > Memory Search.

C4F9E878:EE:00B80090.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
C4F9E878:EE:00B80090.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

Controls how fast the freecam moves while in freecam mode (float, default ~1.0).
Left stick pans, right stick rotates, Circle moves forward, Square moves backward.

CF0B0D11:EE:00F57030.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
CF0B0D11:EE:00F57030.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

D697D204:EE:00F5A020.notes:
Controls how fast the freecam moves while in freecam mode (float, default ~1.0).
Left stick pans, right stick rotates, Circle moves forward, Square moves backward.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify in PCSX2 with Debug > Memory Search.

D697D204:EE:00F5A030.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
D697D204:EE:00F5A030.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

DA5CC7A3:EE:00830064.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
DA5CC7A3:EE:00830064.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

F266B00B:EE:00F55030.description: Freecam toggle button combination — hold all selected buttons simultaneously
F266B00B:EE:00F55030.notes:
Toggle freecam using the selected button combination (press all buttons simultaneously).
When freecam is active:
  • Left analog stick — pan camera (strafe left/right/forward/back)
  • Right analog stick — rotate / tilt camera direction
  • Circle (○)    — move forward in camera facing direction
  • Square (□)    — move backward in camera facing direction
  • Cross (✕)     — descend (move camera down)
  • Triangle (△) — ascend (move camera up)
Press the same combination again to exit freecam and return to normal gameplay.
⚠ Address is research-estimated. Verify with PCSX2 debugger / memory search before use.

── SCE Pad Bitmask Compatibility ──
This game uses the standard Sony SCE libpad library with the normalized
pressed=1 convention, which means:
  ✅ PNACH static writes to camera-mode addresses are supported
  ✅ Button bitmask combo values (L3+R3, L1+L2, etc.) are valid
  ℹ PNACH codes write a FIXED value to memory — they do NOT hook real-time
     input.  To make freecam toggleable via a button press in-game you need
     a conditional (type-C) PNACH code or a separate cheats engine.
  ⚠ Memory address is research-estimated — verify with PCSX2 debugger
     (Debug → Memory Search) before using in production.

── How to use this code ──
In the PNACH Code Builder, select this entry and choose a button combination
from the Combo dropdown.  The builder writes the bitmask value you choose
into the freecam toggle address.  Because PNACH is a static memory writer,
this 'enables' freecam by locking the camera-mode variable at the chosen
value.  To 'disable', load a different PNACH with value 0x00000000.
A proper in-game toggle requires a conditional PNACH (type C) referencing
the live pad bitmask address — advanced use only.

FFAAC65B:EE:00339A7C.description: Motion blur enable flag — toggles full-scene motion blur on/off
FFAAC65B:EE:00339A7C.notes: Boolean flag in Silent Hill 3's graphics config. 0 = disabled (sharper image), 1 = enabled. Address is estimated; verify in PCSX2 via memory scan before use.

FFAAC65B:EE:00339A80.description: Motion blur intensity — controls the strength of the motion blur effect
FFAAC65B:EE:00339A80.notes: Float multiplier (treated as IEEE 754). 0 = none, 1.0 (3F800000) = default. Reduce for subtler blur. Estimated address.

FFAAC65B:EE:00339A84.description: LOD bias — forces a specific mipmap/detail level (lower = highest quality)
FFAAC65B:EE:00339A84.notes: Signed integer or float LOD offset. Negative values force highest-resolution textures. Address is estimated; exact type depends on the game's renderer.

FFAAC65B:EE:00339A88.description: LOD near distance — distance at which highest-quality LOD is shown
FFAAC65B:EE:00339A88.notes: Float. Smaller values keep high-detail models visible from closer. Estimated.

FFAAC65B:EE:00339A8C.description: LOD far distance — distance at which lowest-quality LOD kicks in
FFAAC65B:EE:00339A8C.notes: Float. Larger values keep higher-detail models visible at greater distance. Estimated.

value_map.457A0000: 4000.0 — extended far LOD (higher quality at distance)

FFAAC65B:EE:00339A90.description: Mipmap enable flag — enables or disables mipmap texture filtering
FFAAC65B:EE:00339A90.notes: Boolean flag. 0 = disable mipmaps (can improve sharpness at cost of aliasing). Estimated; verify before applying.

FFAAC65B:EE:00339A94.description: Depth of field enable flag — toggles the depth-of-field blur effect
FFAAC65B:EE:00339A94.notes: Boolean flag in the post-processing configuration. 0 = disabled (crisp), 1 = enabled. Estimated address.

FFAAC65B:EE:00339A98.description: Depth of field intensity — strength of the out-of-focus blur

FFAAC65B:EE:00339A9C.description: Post-processing enable flag — master toggle for post-process effects
FFAAC65B:EE:00339A9C.notes: Boolean. Disabling this flag turns off all post-process effects (bloom, tone-mapping, etc.) for a cleaner, sharper look. Estimated address.

FFAAC65B:EE:00339AA0.description: Bloom / glow intensity — strength of the bloom/HDR glow effect

FFAAC65B:EE:00339AA4.description: Primary draw distance — main camera render distance for world geometry
FFAAC65B:EE:00339AA4.notes: Float (world units). Larger values render geometry further away. Estimated.

FFAAC65B:EE:00339AA8.description: Far draw distance — secondary (far clip) render distance
FFAAC65B:EE:00339AA8.notes: Float (world units). Controls the far clipping plane distance. Estimated.

FFAAC65B:EE:00339AAC.description: Object fade distance — distance at which objects start to pop in/out
FFAAC65B:EE:00339AAC.notes: Float. Higher values make objects appear at greater distances. Estimated.

FFAAC65B:EE:00339AB0.description: Shadow draw distance — how far away shadows are rendered
FFAAC65B:EE:00339AB0.notes: Float. Larger values cast shadows at greater range. Estimated.
